items.q: What does Eagleman mean by a "team of rivals" brain?
items.a: You are not one rational self — **competing neural networks** whose "vote" changes by context. Retrospective regret often means a **different neural party** was driving.

items.q: When does the brain stop changing?
items.a: **Neuroplasticity never fully shuts off** — the brain mainly stops changing when it thinks it already has the world modeled (**crystallized** over fluid). Growth needs attention-intense challenges in the **frustrating-but-achievable** zone.

items.q: What did the Religious Orders Study show about cognitive reserve?
items.a: Nuns with Alzheimer's pathology but **no symptoms** had built **cognitive reserve** from lifelong social/chore challenge. Retirement that shrinks circles and stops pathway-building raises decline risk.

items.q: What is Eagleman's lab theory of REM dreaming?
items.a: **Dream visual-cortex defense** — REM blasts random activity into visual cortex every ~**90 min** to defend visual territory from hearing/touch takeover during darkness. Harvard blindfold: takeover begins in ~**60 min**.

items.q: Do more plastic brains dream more?
items.a: Across **25 primate species**, more plastic brains correlate with **more dream sleep**. Most dream content is noise; meaning is often **post-hoc**, like a random bookshelf sentence.

items.q: How do Ulysses contracts change future-you?
items.a: **Constrain future-you** — clear alcohol from the house, commit to **7 AM** runs with Bob — instead of relying on in-the-moment willpower.

items.q: What enlarges the anterior mid-cingulate (willpower) circuit?
items.a: A history of **hard unwanted work** — not extending tasks you already enjoy. Novice juggling lights up the whole brain; experts show less activity because the brain's goal is **efficiency**.

items.q: What friction should you keep when using AI?
items.a: Outsource **busywork** (vicious friction); never outsource **thinking through novel problems** (virtuous friction). Copy-paste AI answers = no learning plus **effort-phenomenon** red flags.

items.q: How should kids use AI for learning?
items.a: Curiosity-driven Q&A sticks via the plasticity cocktail better than "just in case" schooling. Use AI as **Aristotle-in-pocket**; ask **"why am I wrong?"** — humans still own selection; AI is weak at humor punchlines.

items.q: What renaissance does Eagleman expect post-AI?
items.a: Rising demand for **live theater, live music, in-person talks**, and human care — **live experience** and human connection become economic assets as digital answers get cheap.
